confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (slice-gpi-02 / behaviour-02): on a deep link the title still falls back to 'Ali Bars' at 2x CPU throttle or slower, because the 100ms re-assert timer loses a hydration race
confirmed.expected: Loading /#racing always ends with document.title 'City Racing · Ali Bars' (and /#about ends with 'About · Ali Bars', and so on), whatever the device speed, with no flicker back to 'Ali Bars'.
confirmed.actual: Pile.tsx:62 writes the sheet title and Pile.tsx:63 writes it again after TITLE_REASSERT_MS = 100 (line 28). The write that undoes it comes from react-dom, not from a fixed Next.js timer. React sets nodeValue = 'Ali Bars' on the text node inside the static metadata <title> (layout.tsx:28) when that part of the tree hydrates or commits, and how long that takes depends on CPU speed. At 1x it happens about 41ms after the first write, so the 100ms re-write wins, but the tab title still flickers to 'Ali Bars' for about 77ms. With slower CPUs the React write lands after the re-assert, so the final title is 'Ali Bars'. Results: 2x failed in 1 of 2 runs; 3x (/#video), 4x (/#crumbify), 6x (/#racing, and /#about with the JS chunks delayed by 800ms) and 20x (/#about) all failed. Mid-range phones run at about 4x. The comment at Pile.tsx:49-58 says Next 'reasserts its own static metadata title ~50-100ms after'. That is wrong: the delay is not fixed, so no fixed timeout is robust. The e2e test at e2e/pile.spec.ts:205-212 only passes because the test machine is fast.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on the built out/ with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate. A document.title setter hook plus a MutationObserver gave this timeline for /#racing at 6x: t=4473 doc.title='City Racing · Ali Bars' (Pile effect); t=5053 same value again (100ms timer); t=5150 mutation, title='Ali Bars'. Final page.title() = 'Ali Bars'. Hooking Text.prototype.nodeValue showed the write undoing the title is `nodeValue="Ali Bars"` from react-dom (chunks/4bd1b696-*.js, functions nc > sc > sd > uv). The console showed no errors. At 1x the frame log shows 'City Racing · Ali Bars' at 1653ms, 'Ali Bars' at 1678ms, then 'City Racing · Ali Bars' again at 1755ms.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Use a deterministic approach. Remove `title` from `metadata` in src/app/layout.tsx:28 (keep the openGraph title) and render `<title>{phase === 'done' ? sheetTitles[top] : sheetTitles.cv}</title>` in Pile's JSX. React 19 hoists it into <head>, the static export still contains the default 'Ali Bars' title (extra-gl-33), and React is then the only writer, so nothing races. The comment at Pile.tsx:49-58 only argues against this while the metadata title exists. Another option: keep the metadata and replace the timer with a MutationObserver on the head <title> (childList, characterData, subtree) that writes sheetTitles[top] back whenever the text differs, and disconnect it in the effect cleanup. Add an e2e test that sets Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate to 6, goes to /#racing, waits 3s and expects the title 'City Racing · Ali Bars'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: I reproduced this on the built out/ served on port 5201. I used Playwright with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate and waited 5s after each goto. Results: rate 1 on /#racing gave 'City Racing · Ali Bars' (pass). Rate 4 on /#crumbify gave 'Ali Bars' (fail). Rate 6 on /#racing gave 'Ali Bars' (fail). Rate 6 on /#about gave 'Ali Bars' (fail). The cause is the fixed TITLE_REASSERT_MS=100 at Pile.tsx:28, used by the setTimeout at Pile.tsx:63-65. It is racing the static metadata title at layout.tsx:28 ('Ali Bars'), and a fixed timeout cannot win that race on slow CPUs. The claim in the comment at Pile.tsx:49-58 that Next's reassert comes ~50-100ms later is not a constant. bh-16/intro-16 is not met on mid-range devices.
confirmed.fix: In src/app/layout.tsx:28, remove `title: 'Ali Bars'` from `metadata` and keep openGraph.title. In src/components/Pile.tsx, delete TITLE_REASSERT_MS (line 28) and the effect at lines 59-67, and render `<title>{phase === 'done' ? sheetTitles[top] : 'Ali Bars'}</title>` inside Pile's returned JSX, so React 19 hoists it and is the only writer. Then check that out/index.html still contains <title>Ali Bars</title> (extra-gl-33). If it does not, add a static <title>Ali Bars</title> to the layout <head>, or use a head-title MutationObserver instead of the timer: observe the head <title> with childList/characterData/subtree, write sheetTitles[top] back whenever it differs, and disconnect in cleanup. Also add an e2e test that sets Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate to 6, loads /#racing, waits 3s and expects the title 'City Racing · Ali Bars'.

confirmed.title: New since the round-2 focus fix: dismissing the intro or bringing a sheet from the keyboard draws a 2px black frame around the whole paper sheet
confirmed.expected: Sheets are plain paper with only the spec box-shadow and no border or outline (gl-22). The gl-24 focus outline belongs on interactive controls. The sheet is focused only so the next Tab starts from the right place, and it is not a control.
confirmed.actual: Pile.tsx:79 (after the intro) and Pile.tsx:46 (after bring()) call focus() on the <article tabIndex=-1> sheet (SheetFrame.tsx). After keyboard interaction, the browser's focus-visible heuristic matches, so the global `:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset:2px }` (globals.css:113) draws a black rectangle around the whole A4 sheet. It stays until focus moves again.
confirmed.evidence: On the built site at 1280x900, I focused the title page, pressed Enter and waited 1.5s. document.activeElement was #sheet-cv, matches(':focus-visible') was true, and the computed outline was 'rgb(28, 27, 25) solid 2px', offset 2px. Screenshot: scratchpad/review-r3/slice-global-pile-intro/kbd-cv-outline.png shows a black frame around the CV sheet. After a mouse click, fv=false and there is no frame.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add `article[id^='sheet-']:focus { outline: none; }` in src/components/Sheet.module.css (for example `.sheet:focus-visible { outline: none; }`). The sheet is only a programmatic focus target with tabIndex=-1. Real controls inside it keep the gl-24 outline.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the built site at 1280x900. I tabbed to the div[role=button].js-title-page (third Tab stop), pressed Enter and waited 2s. document.activeElement was ARTICLE#sheet-cv, :focus-visible matched, and the computed outline was solid 2px rgb(28, 27, 25). The screenshot shows a black frame around the whole CV sheet. The focus() calls are at Pile.tsx:79 and :46 on the tabIndex=-1 article (SheetFrame.tsx:27). The outline comes from the global :focus-visible rule at globals.css:113. gl-24 covers interactive elements, and gl-22 defines the sheet with only a box-shadow, so this outline on a non-interactive programmatic focus target is a new visual defect from the round-2 focus fix.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Sheet.module.css, add `.sheet:focus, .sheet:focus-visible { outline: none; }` (the `.sheet` class is applied in SheetFrame.tsx:30). This removes the outline only from the tabIndex=-1 sheet container, and controls inside the sheet keep the gl-24 outline.

confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (slice-gpi-02 / behaviour-02): the deep-link title is still reset to 'Ali Bars' on CPUs 4x or more slower; the 100ms re-assert timer is a race
confirmed.expected: Loading /#crumbify, /#racing, /#video or /#about ends with that sheet's title (for example 'Crumbify · Ali Bars') on any device speed.
confirmed.actual: Next 15.5.26 streams the static metadata title as a separate RSC chunk (`9:{"metadata":[["$","title",..."Ali Bars"]]}` in out/index.html). React commits that chunk some time after Pile's effect, and how long after depends on CPU speed. At 1x the reset lands about 30-40ms after the effect, so the 100ms timer wins. At 4x the reset lands about 450ms after the effect, and at 6x about 330-440ms after, both well after the timer has already fired. document.title then stays 'Ali Bars' for good.
confirmed.evidence: MutationObserver log on the built site with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate. 1x /#crumbify: 231ms 'Crumbify · Ali Bars', 272ms 'Ali Bars', 333ms 'Crumbify · Ali Bars' (passes). 4x /#video after a 12s wait: 1970ms 'Video bot · Ali Bars', 2423ms 'Ali Bars', final 'Ali Bars'. 6x /#crumbify, /#racing and /#about: final 'Ali Bars' in all three (for example 3002ms set, 3438ms reset). 20x: all three final 'Ali Bars'. Only one <title> node exists throughout.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Use a deterministic approach instead of a timer. In the Pile effect, attach a MutationObserver to document.head (childList, subtree, characterData). When document.title !== wanted, set it back to wanted (the check prevents a loop), and disconnect the observer in the effect cleanup. Alternatively, remove `title` from the layout's static `metadata` and put the default <title>Ali Bars</title> in the <head> JSX of layout.tsx, so Next no longer streams a competing title. Either way, add an e2e test that runs with CDP CPU throttling at 6x and checks toHaveTitle after the load settles.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: src/components/Pile.tsx:57-67 sets document.title once, then again once after TITLE_REASSERT_MS=100 (line 28). layout.tsx:28/31 still declares the static metadata title 'Ali Bars', which Next re-commits later. Reproduced live on the built site after an 8s settle. With no throttling, /#crumbify, /#racing and /#about end as 'Crumbify · Ali Bars', 'City Racing · Ali Bars' and 'About · Ali Bars'. With CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 6, all three end as 'Ali Bars'. A fixed delay is a race and cannot be made robust on slow devices.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Pile.tsx, remove the setTimeout/TITLE_REASSERT_MS re-assert. In the title effect, set document.title = wanted and create a MutationObserver on document.head with {childList:true, subtree:true, characterData:true}. Its callback sets document.title = wanted only when document.title !== wanted, which avoids a loop. Disconnect the observer in the effect cleanup. An alternative is to drop `title` from the static metadata in src/app/layout.tsx:28, keeping openGraph.title, and render a plain default <title>Ali Bars</title> in layout's <head> so Next no longer streams a competing title. Add an e2e test that sets CPU throttling to 6x through CDP, loads /#crumbify, waits for the load to settle, and checks toHaveTitle('Crumbify · Ali Bars').

confirmed.title: Mobile (<600px): the whole pile jumps down 72px when the intro ends, because the in-flow tab row mounts only at phase 'done'
confirmed.expected: Dismissing the title page reveals the CV in place. The pile (stage, thickness block, fillers) does not move after the push-in. README says filler sheets and the thickness block never move.
confirmed.actual: At 390px the mobile <Tabs variant='mobile'> row sits in normal flow above .js-stage and only renders when showTabs (phase === 'done'). At the 1000ms pull -> done step it mounts, and the stage jumps from y=91 to y=163 (+72px: two rows of pills plus 12px margin) in a single frame, with no transition.
confirmed.evidence: Scratch mshift.js, viewport 390x844, load '/', wait 2s, click the title page. Stage getBoundingClientRect().y is 91 before the dismiss, 91 at +900ms, and 163 after done. The desktop tabs are position:absolute, so this happens only below 600px.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Reserve the row's space during the intro. Always render the mobile nav (or a placeholder with the same height) and hide it with visibility:hidden or opacity:0 plus pointer-events:none/inert until phase === 'done'. For example, render <Tabs variant='mobile'> unconditionally and pass a `hidden` prop that sets visibility:hidden and aria-hidden while showIntro. The desktop variant can keep mounting only at 'done'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced at a 390x844 viewport. I loaded '/', waited 2s and clicked the title page. The .js-stage rect y was 91 before the click, 91 at +500ms and 163 after phase 'done', a 72px jump in one frame. Pile.tsx:90 mounts the in-flow mobile <Tabs> only when showTabs (phase === 'done'), so the whole pile, including the fillers and thickness block, shifts at the end of the intro. README:218 says fillers never move, and the reveal is meant to happen in place. The mobile row is the recommended layout from README:234, but it is the implementation's own mount timing that makes the pile jump. The desktop tabs are absolutely positioned, so desktop is not affected.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Pile.tsx:90, render the mobile Tabs unconditionally. While showIntro, hide the row with visibility:hidden (or opacity:0), pointer-events:none, inert and aria-hidden, for example through a new `hidden` prop on Tabs that applies a class with visibility:hidden. The row then keeps its height and the stage stays at the same y before and after 'done'. The desktop variant (line 110) can keep mounting only at 'done'.

confirmed.title: Arrow glyphs in Plex Sans text (e.g. 'Here's the team website →') render from Arial via next/font's generated fallback face, not system-ui as in the prototype, and the line is 1px shorter
confirmed.expected: Racing closing line matches the prototype. The → glyph (not in IBM Plex Sans) falls back to system-ui (Segoe UI on Windows, SF on macOS), and the paragraph box is 648.13 x 25.52 at a 760px stage.
confirmed.actual: next/font injects an 'IBM Plex Sans Fallback' @font-face (local Arial with metric overrides) ahead of system-ui, so the missing → glyph is taken from Arial. The paragraph is 648.12 x 24.52 (1px shorter) and the arrow has a different, smaller shape. The same applies to every → or ↗ in sans text (CV highlights, App Store CTA).
confirmed.evidence:
CDP CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode on the Racing '

Here's the team website → csg.racing

': prototype = [Segoe UI x1 glyph, IBM Plex Sans x35]; implementation = [Arial x1 glyph, IBM Plex Sans x35] (scratch fonts.js). Box comparison of all Racing, Video and About children against the served prototype (proto.js) is identical to within 0.01px, except this line: proto height 25.52, impl 24.52. Mono arrows (TikTok ↗) match (Segoe UI Symbol in both).
confirmed.suggestedFix: In src/app/layout.tsx, pass `adjustFontFallback: false` to IBM_Plex_Sans (and to IBM_Plex_Mono and Source_Serif_4 for consistency). The stack then falls through to the globals.css system-ui fallback for glyphs missing from the font, as in the prototype. Alternatively, set `fallback: ['system-ui', 'sans-serif']` so system-ui is tried before the Arial-based adjusted face.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: I ran CDP CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode on the Racing paragraph 'Here's the team website →'. It reports Arial (ArialMT) for 1 glyph and IBM Plex Sans for 35 glyphs. next/font injects `@font-face 'IBM Plex Sans Fallback' { src: local('Arial') ... }` and puts it in --font-plex-sans ahead of the globals.css:43 stack (`var(--font-plex-sans), 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif`). The → glyph therefore never reaches system-ui, which is what both the prototype (`font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',system-ui,sans-serif`) and the project's own stack intend. This is a small but measurable fidelity gap: a different arrow shape and a 1px line-box difference. It affects every →/↗ in sans text.
confirmed.fix: In src/app/layout.tsx, add `adjustFontFallback: false` to the IBM_Plex_Sans options (lines 5-10), and for consistency to IBM_Plex_Mono and Source_Serif_4. Glyphs missing from Plex then fall through to system-ui as globals.css:43 intends. Alternatively, set `fallback: ['system-ui', 'sans-serif']` on IBM_Plex_Sans.

confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (slice-gpi-02 / behaviour-02): deep-link document.title still ends as 'Ali Bars' on slower CPUs; the 100ms re-assert timer loses the race
confirmed.expected: Loading /#racing always ends with document.title 'City Racing · Ali Bars' (and /#about with 'About · Ali Bars'), whatever the device speed.
confirmed.actual: With CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate at 4x, 6x and 10x, /#racing and /#about end with the title 'Ali Bars'. At 20x, /#about also ends with 'Ali Bars'. It only works unthrottled (1x). The title is overwritten after the 100ms re-write has already run.

confirmed.suggestedFix: Make it deterministic and drop the timer. Option A (recommended): remove `title` from the static `metadata` in layout.tsx:28 (keep openGraph.title) and render a React 19 `<title>{sheetTitles[top]}</title>` inside Pile. confirmed.title: Reduced motion: the sheet swap is a hard cut, not a cross-fade (the opacity .2s transition never runs)
confirmed.expected: README Accessibility / bh-13: under prefers-reduced-motion, sheet swaps become an instant cross-fade: the incoming sheet fades its opacity in (Sheet.module.css declares `transition: opacity .2s` for this).
confirmed.actual: useBring starts the reduced-motion move directly at stage 'in', where sheetStyle returns opacity 1. The incoming sheet goes from visibility:hidden at opacity 1 straight to visible at opacity 1 and z 11, so there is no opacity change and nothing fades. The reduced-motion 'out' branch in pile.ts:93 (opacity 0) can never be reached, and REDUCED_SETTLE_MS=200 waits for a transition that never happens.
confirmed.evidence: rm.cjs with reducedMotion:'reduce', per-rAF computed samples after clicking the racing tab: '0ms racing:z0:hidden:op1.00' → '116ms racing:z11:visible:op1.00' → '310ms cv hidden, racing:z10:visible:op1.00'. No frame shows opacity < 1 on either sheet.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Mount the incoming sheet at opacity 0 for one frame (for example, keep a brief 'out' stage of about 1 rAF or 16ms under reduced motion, using the existing opacity:0 branch), then switch it to 'in' so the .2s opacity transition runs. Or fade the outgoing sheet out instead. Add an assertion that some frame shows 0 < opacity < 1.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: README:238 and bh-13 ask for sheet swaps to become an 'instant cross-fade' under reduced motion. The reduced-motion CSS (Sheet.module.css:24-26, transition: opacity .2s) and the useBring doc comment both say the swap should fade. Live with reducedMotion:'reduce', sampled every rAF after a hash change to #racing: racing goes from hidden/op1/z0 to visible/op1/z11 in one frame, and CV goes to hidden at about 255ms. No frame shows opacity below 1 on either sheet, so it is a hard cut with no fade. The cause is usePile.ts:163, which starts at stage 'in' under reduced motion (opacity 1). pile.ts:91-93, the reduced-motion 'out' branch with opacity 0, is unreachable. Severity stays low because 'instant' in the spec is loosely worded.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/usePile.ts useBring, under reduced motion start at stage 'out' (pile.ts already returns STRAIGHT_TRANSFORM, opacity 0, z m+1 for that case, which is invisible and does not move). After one frame (at(16, ...) or a double rAF), switch to stage 'in' (opacity 1, z m+3) so the 0.2s opacity transition runs. Then settle at 16 + REDUCED_SETTLE_MS. Add an e2e assertion that some frame shows 0 < opacity < 1 on the incoming sheet under emulated reduced motion.

confirmed.title: The reduced-motion preference is read once at mount: turning it on mid-session makes the sheet jump instantly off-screen for 440ms

confirmed.actual: resolveIntro() reads matchMedia once in useIntro's mount effect, and nothing listens for later changes. After emulating reduced motion at runtime, CSS removes the transform transition (transition becomes 'opacity 0.2s'), but JS still runs the 'out' stage. The incoming sheet jumps instantly to translate(112%,-3%) rotate(5deg) (off to the right), sits there for 440ms, then jumps back. This is the two-jump behaviour that round-1 behaviour-05 fixed for load-time reduced motion.
confirmed.evidence: rm2.cjs: load /#cv, then page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}), click the racing tab. At 150ms, sheet-racing has inline transform 'translate(112%, -3%) rotate(5deg)', computed matrix(..., 851.2, -32.2) (already at the end position, not interpolating), and computed transition 'opacity 0.2s'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Subscribe to the media query: in usePile, add a matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') 'change' listener that calls setReducedMotion(e.matches), and remove it in cleanup.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: usePile.ts:92-93 reads reduced motion once, in useIntro's mount layout effect (resolveIntro), and nothing listens for later changes. Live: load /#cv, then page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}), then change the hash to #racing. The sheet's computed transition is already 'opacity 0.2s', but JS still runs the 'out' stage. From about 75ms to 475ms, racing sits instantly at matrix(..., 851.2, -32.24) (translate 112%, rotate 5deg) at z9, then jumps back straight at about 542ms. This is the two-jump behaviour round-1 fixed for load-time reduced motion.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/usePile.ts, add an effect in usePile: `const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); const onChange = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setReducedMotion(e.matches); mq.addEventListener('change', onChange); return () => mq.removeEventListener('change', onChange);`. Also add a unit test that fires a change event and checks that the next bring() uses the reduced-motion path.

confirmed.title: NOT-FIXED (slice-gpi-02 / behaviour-02): the deep-link document.title fix is timing-dependent. With 4x or 6x CPU throttling, every deep link still ends on 'Ali Bars'
confirmed.expected: Loading /#racing ends with document.title 'City Racing · Ali Bars', and /#about ends with 'About · Ali Bars', whatever the device speed.
confirmed.actual: The effect writes the title and writes it again 100ms later (TITLE_REASSERT_MS). React-dom then sets nodeValue='Ali Bars' on the Next metadata <title> text node when that node hydrates. On a fast machine this lands about 33ms after the first write, so the 100ms re-write wins. With CPU throttling it lands about 50-250ms after the re-write, so the final title is 'Ali Bars'.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright against out/ served on :5105, with a MutationObserver plus a document.title setter hook. At rate 1, #racing logs [195 SET City Racing, 226 'Ali Bars', 310 SET City Racing] and ends correct. At Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4, #racing logs [1927 SET, 2145 SET (the reassert), 2178 'Ali Bars'] and the final title is 'Ali Bars'. Results: 4x failed 4/4 (#racing and #about), 6x failed 4/4, and 20x was intermittent (#about failed). A stack hook shows the reset is `nodeValue=Ali Bars` written from react-dom (chunks/4bd1b696...js), so React is patching its own metadata <title> node when it hydrates. No console error is emitted. The e2e test at e2e/pile.spec.ts:203-212 runs unthrottled, so it passes on a fast dev box but would be flaky on slow CI runners. Scripts: scratchpad/review-r3/code-quality-security-tests/title.cjs and who.cjs.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Use a deterministic approach instead of a timer. (a) Preferred: remove `title` from `metadata` in src/app/layout.tsx (keep openGraph.title) and render `<title>{phase === 'done' ? sheetTitles[top] : sheetTitles.cv}</title>` inside Pile. React 19 hoists it into <head> during SSR, so the static HTML still has 'Ali Bars', and React owns the only title node, so nothing can overwrite it. (b) Or, in the Pile effect, attach a MutationObserver to document.querySelector('title') ({childList, characterData, subtree}) that re-assigns document.title = wanted whenever it differs, and disconnect it in cleanup. Either way, delete TITLE_REASSERT_MS, and make the e2e test call CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate({rate: 6}) before goto('/#racing') so it would catch this regression.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced against out/ on :5205 using a Playwright CDP session with Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate and a 4s settle. At rate 1, #racing gave 'City Racing · Ali Bars' and #about gave 'About · Ali Bars'. At rate 4 and at rate 6, both #racing and #about ended on 'Ali Bars' (4/4 fail). Pile.tsx:59-67 relies on one setTimeout(TITLE_REASSERT_MS=100), so the result depends on timing. layout.tsx:28 metadata.title='Ali Bars' is the conflicting node. The e2e test at pile.spec.ts:203-212 runs unthrottled, so it cannot catch this.
confirmed.fix: Make the title deterministic. Preferred: in src/components/Pile.tsx, inside the phase==='done' effect, set document.title = wanted and attach a MutationObserver to document.head with {childList:true, subtree:true, characterData:true}. Its callback re-assigns document.title = wanted whenever document.title !== wanted, and the effect cleanup disconnects it. Delete TITLE_REASSERT_MS and the setTimeout. Alternative: remove `title` from metadata in src/app/layout.tsx (keep openGraph.title) and render <title>{phase==='done' ? sheetTitles[top] : 'Ali Bars'}</title> from Pile, so there is only one title node. Verify that the static out/index.html still contains <title>Ali Bars</title>. Also update e2e/pile.spec.ts:203: open a CDP session, send Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate({rate:6}) before goto('/#racing'), and keep the 1100ms wait plus the toHaveTitle assertion.
